articles.headline: Sources: Giants QB Jaxson Dart out for extended period
articles.description: Jaxson Dart's knee injury is more severe than originally anticipated, and the Giants QB could miss the rest of the season, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo.
articles.body:
Jaxson Dart could miss the rest of the season after tests showed that the New York Giants quarterback's knee injury is more severe than initially anticipated, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo.

Dart suffered the injury during the opening possession of Monday's 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams. Coach John Harbaugh said after the game that the Giants likely avoided a "devastating outcome" with Dart's knee.

But sources told Rapoport and Garafolo that the second-year star will miss an extended period of time and is facing the possibility of season-ending surgery.

Harbaugh said Monday that evaluations on Dart's knee were still ongoing and declined to comment further on his timeline to return.

"It's an ongoing conversation about the health of a player, of a person," Harbaugh said on a video call with reporters. "We've got to prepare for the range of possibilities."

Harbaugh also expressed confidence in backup quarterback Jameis Winston's ability to step in for however long Dart is sidelined.

The Giants lost Dart on their seventh snap of the game, when he was hit on his right side by Rams linebacker Byron Young. That hit sent Dart into linebacker Josaiah Stewart, who undercut the quarterback's legs, resulting in a hard fall.

Dart immediately grabbed at his left knee and went to the blue medical tent. He walked with a limp to the locker room and initially was listed as questionable to return to the game before officially being ruled out early in the third quarter.

Winston struggled in place of Dart, completing 11 of 27 passes for 111 yards and an interception.

Beyond Winston, the Giants have quarterback Jake Haener on their practice squad. But with Dart expected to miss an extended period, Harbaugh and the Giants will lean on Winston, who signed a two-year, $13 million contract extension earlier this month.

Dart, 23, flashed promise as a rookie last year and was outstanding in New York's season-opening victory over the Dallas Cowboys, completing 23 of 29 passes for 230 yards and three touchdowns while also rushing for 54 yards.

articles.headline: Packers lose RT Zach Bako-Bewele to season-ending surgery
articles.description: Packers RT Zach Bako-Bewele, considered the team's best offensive lineman, is set to undergo knee surgery that will sideline him for 8-10 months.
articles.body:
GREEN BAY, Wis. -- For the second straight season, the Green Bay Packers have lost right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele for the season due to a torn patellar tendon in his right knee.

Last year, it was a partial tear that prevented him from coming back after he was injured in Week 15. This year, he said it was a complete tear sustained in Sunday's overtime win over the New York Jets.

Bako-Bewele, who was limited most of the offseason while recovering from a surgery he described as a repair to remove some tissue around the patellar tendon, now will undergo a more complex surgery that expects to sideline him for 8-10 months. He said the surgery is scheduled for Thursday.

 

He would not say whether he may have come back too soon from the initial surgery. He did not rule out that the surface at MetLife Stadium may have played a role.

"I don't know," Bako-Bewele said Tuesday. "I mean, I don't think the turf helped. Yeah, I don't know. Just something that happened, so I just gotta move forward."

The fourth-round pick in 2022 is widely considered the Packers' best offensive lineman. They signed him to a four-year, $88 million contract extension in 2025. Second-year pro Anthony Belton finished Sunday's game at right tackle and likely will start there again Thursday against the Atlanta Falcons.

That wasn't the only injury on the offensive line from Sunday's game. They finished the game without left guard Aaron Banks (toe/knee) and then lost his replacement Donovan Jennings to a hand injury. Rookie Jager Burton finished the game at left guard. He was the last offensive lineman available in the game and when right guard Jacob Monk was getting evaluated for a stinger, the Packers were preparing to use tight end Tucker Kraft at one of the offensive line spots.

The Packers have struggled to run the ball, ranking last in rushing yards per game (64.5) and 29th in yards per carry (3.3).

They also lost receiver Jayden Reed to what was initially called a neck injury but according to ESPN's Adam Schefter was actually a back injury. It's unclear how much time, if any, Reed will miss. He returned to Green Bay on Monday after being held in New Jersey after the game for observation.

articles.headline: Spain refs back Real, say Lee deserved red for Valverde tackle
articles.description: Spain's Technical Committee of Referees said Lee Kang-In should have been sent off in Sunday's Madrid derby, while backing the decision not to show Cristian Romero a red card.
articles.body:
Spain's Technical Committee of Referees said Lee Kang-In should have been sent off in Sunday's Madrid derby, while backing the decision not to show Cristian Romero a red card.

Atlético Madrid won the high-profile LaLiga clash 2-1 at the Metropolitano, but Real Madrid coach José Mourinho slammed referee Miguel Ortiz Arias afterwards, bringing printed-out photos to his post-match news conference to back his claim both players should have been dismissed.

Lee's challenge on Federico Valverde -- which resulted in the Madrid midfielder suffering a grade three ankle sprain that forced him out of Uruguay's squad for their upcoming friendlies -- and Romero's clash with Jude Bellingham, treading on the England star's knee, both came in the first half with the game tied at 0-0.

Lee went unpunished, while Romero was shown a yellow card after Bellingham had initially been booked before the VAR intervened.

In its weekly review of controversial refereeing decisions released on Tuesday, the CTA assessed those two incidents, as well as a red card for Madrid's Dean Huijsen, which resulted in a penalty Atlético converted to open the scoring.

The CTA first analysed the Huijsen sending off, saying the defender had "grabbed the arm" of Atlético forward Giuliano Simeone, "without the possibility of playing the ball" and that the eventual decision of a red card, after a VAR check, was correct.

It then looked at the Lee challenge, saying there was a "high risk of injury" for Valverde and the failure of Ortiz Arias to show the Atlético player a red card was a "clear and obvious error" which the VAR should have corrected.

The CTA also said that the VAR had acted correctly in intervening to ensure that Romero was shown a yellow card.

After Sunday's game, Mourinho slammed both the referee and the VAR, saying Ortiz Arias "couldn't cope with the pressure" and saying the VAR had a "big history" with Real Madrid.

The loss for Mourinho's Madrid left them in fourth place in LaLiga, six points behind leaders Barcelona after seven games.

articles.headline: Fantasy football flex and superflex rankings for Week 3
articles.description: Trying to decide between a couple of closely ranked players this week? Eric Karabell's rankings are here to help.
articles.body:
Welcome to Week 3 of the 2026 NFL season and our weekly PPR fantasy football superflex rankings. We know many of you compete in superflex formats that invite/covet second quarterbacks in starting lineups, and these rankings account for that. It might look odd to see the lowest-ranked fantasy passers ahead of typical RB2 and WR2 options, but the potential scoring impact demands it.

If your league is a standard flex, note that rankings without QBs appear below the superflex rankings. However you prefer to play, good luck this week!

Jump to a section:

Superflex rankings (with QBs)

Standard flex rankings (RBs, WRs, TEs only)

-->These ranks have been refreshed to take out players from Thursday's Falcons-Packers game.

-->

Week 3 superflex rankings (includes quarterbacks)

 1. Josh Allen, QB1 vs LAC

He probably cannot average 38.2 fantasy points per game for long, but he belongs in his own tier.

 2. Jahmyr Gibbs, RB1 vs NYJ

As long as each Lions game is a shootout, there is nothing to worry about here.

 3. Jaxon Smith-Njigba, WR1 @ WSH

Perhaps last season wasn't a fluke. He is doing it again, regardless of quarterback.

 4. Kenneth Walker III, RB2 @ MIA

We have never seen him play like this before, with this much volume. Just. Stay. Healthy.

 5. Amon-Ra St. Brown, WR2 vs NYJ

Nobody has more targets than this fellow. We expected more of a split with Jameson Williams.

 6. Christian McCaffrey, RB3 vs ARI

Low volume is not a concern yet, but it will be if he doesn't score touchdowns.

 7. Jonathan Taylor, RB4 vs HOU

It sure looks like last season was not a fluke for him. The touchdowns keep on coming.

 8. Lamar Jackson, QB2 @ DAL

He wasn't awesome in Week 2, but this week, it is the Cowboys. He should be awesome.

 9. Brock Purdy, QB3 vs ARI

Enjoy this week versus Arizona. Then he faces the Broncos and Seahawks.

 10. Jalen Hurts, QB4 @ CHI

The Eagles' offense remains in flux, but Hurts is not a problem.

 11. Patrick Mahomes, QB5 @ MIA

 12. Tyler Shough, QB6 vs LV

 13. Puka Nacua, WR3 @ DEN

A hip injury cost him Week 2. At least the Rams don't play on Monday this week.

 14. Ja'Marr Chase, WR4 @ PIT

Magnificent player who needs to produce those Week 2 numbers more often. He needs more volume.

 15. Justin Jefferson, WR5 @ TB

 16. Chris Olave, WR6 vs LV

 17. CeeDee Lamb, WR7 vs BAL

 18. Derrick Henry, RB5 @ DAL

The Ravens underutilized him in the second half last week, which makes no sense.

 19. Bijan Robinson, RB6 @ GB

Thursday is a big game for his fantasy value, but can we really doubt this guy?

 20. Dak Prescott, QB7 vs BAL

 21. Joe Burrow, QB8 @ PIT

 22. Jordan Love, QB9 vs ATL

We didn't expect to rank him so well, but quite a few backup QBs are starting this week.

 23. Trevor Lawrence, QB10 vs NE

Underwhelming Week 2 versus a tough opponent, so he gets a pass. But he needs to run more.

 24. De'Von Achane, RB7 vs KC

He did have 23 touches in Week 2. We cannot expect his 2025 numbers, but don't give up on him.

articles.headline: Nacua and Bowers lead fantasy football Knockout league pickups for Week 3
articles.description: Tristan H. Cockcroft lists the most common players on eliminated teams and finds how much FAB to spend this week.
articles.body:
Injuries are the great equalizer in sports.

They can prove especially devastating in fantasy football knockout leagues.

On Monday night, New York Giants QB Jaxson Dart became the second quarterback in as many weeks to suffer a game-ending injury within the first 11 snaps while scoring fewer than one fantasy point (0.80), joining Kyler Murray (Week 1). Unsurprisingly -- though it's worth pointing out that he was facing a difficult matchup against the Los Angeles Rams -- Dart resided on the largest percentage of teams knocked out for Week 2, with an even higher rate than anyone had the week before (19.6%).

Dart wasn't alone. Philadelphia Eagles RB Saquon Barkley, who played only 10 snaps (14% of the Eagles' total on offense) and 3.0 fantasy points, was the most commonly knocked out running back for the second consecutive week. Along with those two, the top 10 names on this week's list also included Caleb Williams and DJ Moore, who left their respective contests early due to injuries, as well as Nico Collins (hamstring), Puka Nacua (hip), Brock Bowers (knee) and A.J. Brown (ankle), all of whom were ruled out in advance of their respective games.

It's a factor in the knockout format that'll ring louder with each passing week.

As teams get eliminated and your active managerial pool shrinks, rosters strengthen and injury-influenced lineup holes increasingly sink your team in the standings. It's something to keep in mind as you evaluate the downside risk of your weekly lineup.

Yes, some injuries can be chalked up to bum luck -- for a great historical example, no one could've foreseen Tom Brady tearing his ACL in 2008's opening week -- but others can be reasonably forecasted. In Dart's case,  we  warned  you about his downside risks, which made him a disadvantageous pick in the knockout format.

Dart's injury underscores another critical factor for knockout play: Stacking, as his top wide receiver, Malik Nabers, scored only 1.1 fantasy points while working most of the day with backup Jameis Winston. It's the second time in Nabers' past four games played that he has delivered a miserable, sub-four-point score terribly sunk by poor quarterback play (3.3 in Week 3 of 2025, with Russell Wilson as his quarterback). And with Tuesday's report that Dart might miss the remainder of the season, Nabers is probably looking at more low-floor scores like those. 

Tying your wide receiver's result to your quarterback's can prove dangerous, especially if either -- and in this case both -- carries an injury question.

That's not to say that you cannot stack! Outcomes like Dak Prescott's 29.76 and CeeDee Lamb's 35.3 fantasy point Week 2 working together are plenty welcome across all fantasy leagues, but remember, it's floor, not ceiling, that's the goal in knockout play.

To that end, in the Fantasy Focus Podcast Knockout league, this week's knocked out team started both Dart and Nabers. A team projected before Monday Night Football to survive by 21.5 fantasy points

articles.headline: Raptors agree to 2-year, $115M extension with Kawhi Leonard
articles.description: Toronto Raptors star Kawhi Leonard has agreed on a two-year, $115 million contract extension with the franchise, plus a player option for the 2028-29 season, his agent Harrison Gaines of SLASH Sports told ESPN on Tuesday.
articles.body:
Toronto Raptors star Kawhi Leonard has agreed on a two-year, $115 million contract extension with the franchise, plus a player option for the 2028-29 season, his agent Harrison Gaines of SLASH Sports told ESPN on Tuesday.

Both sides maintained consistent dialogue on Leonard's long-term Raptors future since July - with the two-time Finals MVP expecting to finish his career in Toronto. Leonard, 35, now has a total of three years and $165 million on his Raptors deal.

Leonard took $11 million less than his maximum extension number - on top of waiving a $7.45 million trade kicker to accommodate his trade from the LA Clippers - as the sides discussed flexibility for the Raptors' rising salary books.

On June 30, the Raptors and Clippers agreed on a trade sending Leonard back to Toronto for Brandon Ingram, Gradey Dick, two unprotected first-round picks, one first-round pick swap and two second-rounders. The deal was placed on pause when the NBA informed the Raptors in early July that the franchise would be liable for any discipline for Leonard amid the league's investigation into salary cap circumvention allegations for the Clippers, clearing the way for both Toronto and LA to wait on the outcome of the probe.

The NBA announced earlier this month a list of severe punishments for the Clippers, including the loss of five future first-round picks, a fine of $30 million and a yearlong suspension for owner Steve Ballmer for violating salary cap circumvention rules in a case involving Leonard, who paid $700,000 in restitution for improper benefits provided by the franchise for his uncle and former business representative, Dennis Robertson.

Leonard fired Robertson and agent Mitch Frankel in June and hired Gaines weeks later. Robertson has been banned by the NBA from all business dealings.

The NBA's punishments came down after nearly a yearlong investigation into the franchise that "found a pattern of misconduct and multiple significant rules violations by the Clippers organization, a prior offender of the salary cap circumvention rules."

Leonard led the Raptors to their first NBA championship in franchise history in 2019 before leaving Toronto the following offseason to sign with the Clippers.

Leonard, who turned 35 in June, is coming off the highest-scoring season of his career, averaging 27.9 points for the Clippers in 65 games. He is a seven-time All-Star, seven-time All-NBA selection, a two-time NBA champion and two-time Finals MVP (winning in 2019 with Toronto and 2014 with San Antonio) and is generally considered one of the game's top defensive players.

articles.descriptionJa: ペッレ・ラーションがヒートと長期延長契約を結んだ件を含め、NBA全体の契約、トレード、噂を追跡しています。
articles.body:
NBA free agency has almost reached the end, with several players landing in new homes this offseason.

LeBron James decided to continue his historic career with the Philadelphia 76ers after months of deliberation. The Sixers also traded for Jaylen Brown this summer, turning the franchise into a true contender with two huge moves.

Meanwhile, Giannis Antetokounmpo is headed to South Beach to team up with Bam Adebayo and the Miami Heat, and the Los Angeles Lakers have been sold for the second time in 10 months.

What will happen next during this turbulent offseason?

Check back here for all the latest buzz, news and reactions from our ESPN NBA insiders, with the latest info at the top:

Quick links:

Free agency grades | Trade grades

Trade tracker | Transactions

Depth charts | Trade machine | More

Sept. 22

Leonard, Raptors agree to two-year extension

The Toronto Raptors and Kawhi Leonard have agreed to a two-year, $115 million extension, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Leonard now has a total of three years and $165 million left on his deal.

The 2026-27 season will be Leonard's first back in Toronto since the 2018-19 campaign, a season in which he helped lead the Raptors to their only title in franchise history.

Sept. 21

Charania: Pistons, Duren at an "impasse"

Free agent center Jalen Duren and the Detroit Pistons are at an impasse this season and the franchise is uncertain if he will show up to next Monday's Media Day, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania.

"When you talk to people close to [Duren], he feels a certain way toward the Pistons' respect level for him," Charania said on NBA Today. "For him it's been all about respect, for the team it has just been about business. ... Over the course of this offseason, his offer has been been around the $180 to $190 million over five years range. And that has also included incentives like weight clauses to my understanding. And that has all played a part in this as well.

"Over the last several weeks it's kind of quiet on this front. The sides have picked up communication. And I am told right now the Pistons offer to Jalen Duren is $200 million over five years."

Duren has until Oct. 1 to sign a qualifying offer.

Hawks' Henri Veesaar out with torn ACL

The Atlanta Hawks announced that center Henri Veesaar tore his ACL during a Sept. 15 workout. He will undergo surgery in October and is expected to miss the entire 2026-27 season.

Sept. 18

Pistons, Thompson reach five-year, $155 million extension

Detroit Pistons All-Defensive forward Ausar Thompson has agreed to a five-year, $155 million rookie-scale contract extension with the franchise, sources told ESPN.

Thompson lands the fully guaranteed extension after making first-team All-Defense and finishing third in Defensive Player of the Year voting last season. The 23-year-old averaged 9.9 points, 5.7 rebounds, 3.1 assists and 0.9 blocks in 2025-26 while leading the NBA in steals per game (2.0).
